I have been farming this land my whole life, since I was a young girl helping my parents. My husband and I have 6 mu of flat field here in Quzhou. Now my children are in the city — my son works in Shijiazhuang — so I farm mostly alone, with help from my neighbor's family during the busy harvest.

I do not need to think hard about what to grow. Every year is the same. Winter wheat goes in the ground in October, comes out in June. Then I plant summer maize right after, in the same fields. This is what my parents did, what everyone in the village does. The soil here knows wheat and maize. I know wheat and maize.

I will buy seeds from the supply shop in town. The man there knows me. He will have the same good maize seed as last year — the hybrid one. For wheat I will use the improved seed the village sold us last season; I kept back a little but I will buy fresh too because the kept seed gets weaker.

For fertilizer, I will apply the diammonium phosphate as a base before planting wheat, then chase with urea at jointing. My neighbor Old Liu uses more urea than me and his wheat looks the same, but urea is money. I will use what I have always used.

The well is shared. I will pump three times for wheat — once before winter sets in, once when the stalks stretch up, once when the grain is filling. Maize gets rain in summer mostly; I will pump once if July is dry like it was two years ago.

I keep a small patch near the house — one mu — for garlic and cabbage. This is for eating and for the market in town. My daughter-in-law likes when I send garlic.
